newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac "calmly" consults French political leaders.
newsitem.headline: Chirac "calmly" consults French political leaders.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac was consulting political leaders "calmly" by telephone on Monday on the outcome of Sunday's parliamentary election first round in which the left strongly outpolled his centre-right coalition.
Officials in Chirac's office said he was studying the results and holding telephone consultations in a "calm, studious and thoughtful" atmosphere.

Chirac left his busy official schedule for Monday unchanged despite the election results, which could leave him the lame-duck prisoner of a Socialist and Communist parliamentary majority if the voting pattern is repeated in next Sunday's runoff round.

The president's office said he would lunch with Abu Dhabi crown prince Sheikh Khalifa bin Zaid al-Nahayan before holding separate meetings with NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana and Russian President Boris Yeltsin in the late afternoon ahead of a NATO-Russia summit in Paris on Tuesday.
Aides to Chirac gave no hint of whether he was considering replacing Prime Minister Alain Juppe after Sunday's massive protest vote against austerity and record unemployment.
Juppe said on Monday he was convinced Chirac would make the right choice if a change of personality was the only obstacle to the centre-right coalition winning the runoff.
